critiques.summary:
Round 2 resolved both blocking issues from my round-1 review.

(a) Change-uniqueness now tested beyond the standard feeds. T4 explicitly probed the shared deps (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka, portfolio-service): config feed 0 for all, deployment feed 0 for ledger-db/portfolio-service, and the agent confirmed no separate infra/ops/maintenance feed or margin-datastore entity exists in the tool namespace (F20,F21,F23). So the residual "invisible infra change" path is not merely unqueried — it is not queriably observable at all; the only residual is a strictly unobservable event whose signature (immediate NPE inside a brand-new validator) no infra degradation explains.

(b) The truncated-log weakness is gone: the full 426/426 ERROR population is now reconciled by pattern counts summing exactly to each sub-window total (224 NPE/FNO + 202 "marginProfile is null"), 'equity' search returned 0 (F31-F34), and the exclusivity caveat is now honest (metric has no order-type dimension; logs are the sole source).

(c) H2 was actually tested, not dismissed: the only plausible marginProfile owner (portfolio-service) is flat on error_rate, p99 and logs with no step at 12:10-12:12Z, and no margin-service/profile-store exists in known_services (F25,F26,F27,F28,F29,F30). H3 was tested via the shared-dep feeds plus ledger-db connections flat. H4 is refuted by flat resource metrics and flat request_rate (F11,F17,F18,F36).

Remaining issues are honest secondary details, not origin-separating: the null's provenance (code path vs pre-existing sparse data) is untraced, the owner of the lookup is inferred, and no revert-recovery was observed. All three live inside the same origin (the new validation path deployed by dep-5101), so they lower confidence rather than change the ranking or the fix.

Temporal order is tight (deploy 12:10:00Z; onset bucket 12:10Z, first error 12:12:31Z; sustained). Scope is clean: order-service steps, api-gateway merely reflects the 5xx, every other service flat. No surviving competitor names a different origin with supporting evidence.

challenges.issue: The provenance of the null marginProfile is untraced: it is asserted to be produced by the new code path itself, but F9 only shows the null is observed there. A pre-existing sparse/missing data record for F&O accounts (a data-population issue) would be a different remediation than a missing null guard. Mitigated because both mechanisms sit inside the dep-5101 validation change, which is still the change to revert/hotfix, and because the onset is exactly at deploy time, which argues against a long-standing data gap.

The exact component served by MarginCheckValidator's marginProfile lookup is inferred (no margin/profile dependency appears in the dependency graph and no margin-service exists). Portfolio-service is only a candidate owner, so its health is suggestive rather than dispositive for eliminating H2.

No recovery evidence: dep-5101 is still live with no rollback through 13:59Z, so the decisive revert-restores-baseline confirmation was never observed. Correlation plus mechanism plus elimination of alternatives is strong but not a controlled reversal.

F&O exclusivity rests on logs alone (no order-type metric dimension exists), and each log page returned truncated:true; a rare non-FNO entry could hide in unreturned middles. Argued against by pattern counts summing exactly to sub-window totals (F31,F32), so low residual risk.

H3 is eliminated partly by absence of a queryable feed rather than by positive measurement of shared-dep health (ledger-db slow_queries_per_min, redis-cache hit_ratio/evictions, kafka metrics never retrieved). The absence is structural (no such feed exists) and the one positive shared-dep metric (connections_active) is flat, so this does not re-rank H3, but it is why confidence is capped below 0.9.
